topic: مدى أثر القرارات المالية الحكومية الأجنبية على الشراكات والشركات في مصر: قراءة قانونية
prompt: A modern, well‑lit office conference room. A rectangular glass table occupies the center of the frame, surrounded by four professionals—two men and two women in business‑casual attire, all appearing to be Egyptian (skin tone, facial features, subtle cultural cues such as a simple necklace or a modest haircut). One person (a man in his forties) leans forward, his right hand pointing at a thick contract spread open on the table; the contract’s pages show highlighted sections and a thick red “Force Majeure” stamp visible without needing to read the text. Across from him, a woman in her thirties holds a printed newspaper‑style sheet with a bold headline about “foreign government financial restrictions” and a small foreign flag graphic in the corner; the sheet displays a chart of currency flows, again recognizable without readable text. In the middle of the table, an open laptop displays a news website on a foreign government’s finance ministry page—visible are a logo, a graph with rising arrows, and a small flag icon, all clearly indicating an external financial decision. Another man, seated at the far end, looks thoughtfully at a tablet that shows a contract clause titled “Change of Law” highlighted in yellow, his left hand resting on his chin. A large window behind the group lets in soft natural daylight, complemented by subtle overhead LED lighting that creates even illumination across the table. The composition is a straight‑on, eye‑level shot that captures the entire table and the four participants, emphasizing the interaction between the contract documents, the foreign‑financial‑decision evidence, and the concerned business owners.
